title: Isolate a divisible pivot by invertible matrix operations
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, m ∈ ℕ, D a square matrix indexed by Fin (m + 1) over R, and r,c : Fin (m + 1). Assume that p = D(r,c) divides every entry of D. Then there exist square matrices P,Q indexed by Fin (m + 1), invertible under matrix multiplication, and a square matrix C indexed by Fin m, such that P D Q has entry p at (0,0), zero at every (0,j.succ) and (i.succ,0), and entry C(i,j) at every (i.succ,j.succ). No nonvanishing or determinant hypothesis is required.
lean_statement: ∀ (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (m : ℕ) (D : Matrix (Fin (m + 1)) (Fin (m + 1)) R) (r c : Fin (m + 1)), (∀ i j, D r c ∣ D i j) → ∃ (P Q : Matrix (Fin (m + 1)) (Fin (m + 1)) R) (C : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) R), IsUnit P ∧ IsUnit Q ∧ P * D * Q = Matrix.of (fun i j => Fin.cases (Fin.cases (D r c) (fun _ => 0) j) (fun i' => Fin.cases 0 (fun j' => C i' j') j) i)
